Learned counsel for the appellant submits that allegation of violating privacy of 2 CRA-8283-2023 victim (P.W.-2) is factually incorrect.

Firstly, prosecution did not deem it proper to seek identification of appellant-Dadulal Kol and exhibit the TIP carried out in the hands of the witness Dadulal Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143036542/

sentences.text: It is submitted that trial Court has completely overlooked the cross-examination of this witness (PW-2) who has deposed that she was earlier not knowing Dadulal.
She had no meeting with Dadulal.
Incident took place at 11.30 p.m.
She was in her hutment.
There is no light in the hutment nor any other source of light.
It is correct that at 11.30 p.m. it was pitch dark.
It is correct that when incident took place, she was alone.
She was not carrying torch at that time and later on her husband had come with a torch.
It is correct that persons who violated her privacy had ran away and her husband had reached the spot with a torch later on.
She could not make out as to who had given effect to the incident.
Some persons came who had committed the offence.

Reading this cross-examination, it is submitted that it is evident that victim (P.W.-2) is talking of some Langad alias Langda and there is no material on record to show appellant-Dadulal Kol is the same person i.e. Langad alias Langda.
It is also submitted that appellant is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter.
There are good chances of success in this appeal.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail.
Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State, in his turn, opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Without commenting on the merits of the case and taking this fact into consideration that even prosecution has not bothered to exhibit the TIP, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail.
Accordingly, I.A.No.17474/2025 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 19.11.2025 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court,
which shall not be more than two times in a year, the execution of remaining part of the jail sentence imposed upon appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of this appeal.
List this appeal for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(VIVEK AGARWAL)
